$comment: Every entry is keyed on a SITE -- (table, column, file) -- and NEVER on a
column name alone. `column` is the OLD name the alias targets. A name-keyed
entry here would be the stoplist that hid
which returned 129 findings with not one of them `total` over a rename that
wiped a year of projection values.
An entry that no longer suppresses anything is reported as a FINDING, so a
repaired or migrated site forces its entry out rather than leaving a standing
exemption for the name. Do not add an entry to quiet a gate you have not read.
verdict = keep-aliased     the alias is a deliberate boundary translation and
migrating it would move a name the gate cannot see
the consumers of (a wire contract, an SPA key).
The reason must name the consumer that fixes it.
verdict = migrate-tracked  the alias should go, and the migration is tracked
elsewhere. The reason must name where.

adjudications.reason: This explicit projection IS the wire contract, and it was added deliberately in response to the failure this gate exists to catch: app/core/percentiles/reducer.js spreads the row straight into redux and percentile-metric.js plus stacked-metric.js read .p25/.p75/.min/.max, so a prior rename that let the physical names through collapsed the color arithmetic to NaN || 0. Migrating it is an SPA-visible rename, not a server change. The new-name key reads the gate lists (libs-shared/simulation/simulation-utils.mjs, scripts/generate-nfl-team-seasonlogs.mjs) are a different population -- they build percentile objects from their own computation and never read a row from this route.

Adjudicated MIGRATE, tracked in user:task/league/migrate-roster-row-position-and-roster-id-to-physical-names.md. It is a shared-class API rename across 55+ call sites reaching libs-shared/roster.mjs and the SPA, so it is sequenced behind this gate rather than folded into it -- the gate is the instrument that makes the migration auditable. This entry falls out when that task ships. CLASS NOTE, rewritten 2026-08-20: the producer set is GATE-DERIVED and larger than the hand-written list this note used to carry. The 2026-08-06 note named three producers off a bare side that read only projection arguments; the gate now also counts a statement with NO projection call, which emits every column of rosters_players under its physical names, and this pair's producer count is 22. Line numbers are deliberately absent from this reason -- the adjudication key is (table, column, file) precisely BECAUSE lines decay, and all three the old note cited had already drifted. The producers are cited as greppable shapes instead, each opened and each reading the PHYSICAL name end to end, so none is a live defect: libs-server/simulation/compute-actuals-optimal-lineup.mjs selects 'player_position' and reads row.player_position in its `for (const row of roster_rows)` loop; scripts/generate-tag-board.mjs selects 'player_position' and its only `pos:` is `pos: row.primary_position`, taken off a db('player') row, a different table; scripts/calculate-franchise-tag.mjs selects 'rosters_players.*' wholesale and then groupBy(rosters, 'player_position'), reading no short name; the balance are projection-less wholesale reads of rosters_players. They are the divergent-vocabulary surface the tracked migration has to sweep, not a defect standing today.

UNIFORM in substance FOR THE points-map SHAPE: both producers of that row -- this file and scripts/process-projections-for-league-format.mjs -- alias back, and get_player_week_total (libs-shared/get-player-week-points.mjs:16-21) reads .total off each week's row. This is the column whose UNALIASED select wiped a year of projection values in 72346e579, so the alias is the repair rather than the residue. The new-name key reads the gate lists (scripts/process-projections-for-scoring-format.mjs:82,99) are the WRITER's insert payload, a different boundary that never reads a row from this select. Removing the alias means moving get_player_week_total and every consumer of the points map in the same change. SCOPE CAUTION, added 2026-08-06 by adversarial review: this reason is NOT a claim that only two sites query this table. libs-server/simulation/load-data-with-fallback.mjs:172 aliases the same column to a THIRD name (`as projection`) and reads it bare at :294, and libs-server/simulation/load-projection-data.mjs:121-133 selects and reads the physical name directly. Those feed different downstream shapes, not player.points[week].total, and none is gate-visible (an alias to `projection` targets no lost column). A future rename of this column must sweep libs-server/simulation/ and cannot rely on this entry as an inventory. CLASS NOTE, 2026-08-06: now SPLIT PRODUCERS rather than ORPHANED ALIAS, naming libs-server/simulation/load-projection-data.mjs:128 as the bare producer -- which is the site the SCOPE CAUTION above already identified by hand. It selects the physical name and reads it directly, feeding a different downstream shape than player.points[week].total, so the verdict is unchanged and the class change is the gate catching up to the caution.

The second producer of the same shape, and its own comment records why: get_player_week_total reads .total, so an unaliased select hands every player NaN which becomes the -999 sentinel, and the writer below deletes by (league_format_id, year) before inserting. Both producers OF THE points-map SHAPE agree. The gate reports this as SPLIT PRODUCERS rather than UNIFORM as of 2026-08-06, naming libs-server/simulation/load-projection-data.mjs:128 -- which selects the physical name for a different downstream shape and is exactly the site the SCOPE CAUTION below already named by hand. The bare producer does not feed the points map, so the verdict stands.
